_readme: Copy of the defaults used to seed config/sources.json on first run. This file IS tracked in git; config/sources.json is NOT (see .gitignore) -- it holds machine-local paths and hostnames and is generated from this file automatically the first time the dashboard starts. Edit config/sources.json directly for your own machine; edit this file only if you want to change what a fresh install starts with. `refresh_preset` is 'normal' (the intervals_s below, unchanged) or 'relaxed' (roughly 3x longer -- for a laptop on battery); it is a multiplier over intervals_s, not a second set of numbers. `allow_config_writes` (default true) gates POST /api/config/layout and POST /api/config/theme -- the settings panel needs it true to save changes; set it false if you bind this dashboard beyond 127.0.0.1 (e.g. bind_host 0.0.0.0 on a LAN) and want it read-only from the browser. `disk_mounts` (default ["/"]) is the list of mounts the system panel reports on, local and remote; a mount that doesn't exist on a given host is skipped, not a failure. `collectors` (default {}, meaning auto-detect everything) lets you force a collector on or off regardless of auto-detection, e.g. {"beads": {"enabled": false}} -- a collector whose optional dependency (bd/~/.overlord/an ssh host) is absent starts inactive on its own and is re-checked every `collector_redetect_interval_s` seconds, so e.g. installing bd later brings its panel alive with no restart. `update_repo` is empty by default -- the dashboard's own upstream repo is private, so leaving this unset avoids a third-party install's update check 404ing against a repo it can't read; set it to your own fork's "owner/repo" to enable GET /api/update/check and POST /api/update/apply (also requires allow_self_update: true). `bd_bin`/`herdr_bin` below are this repo's own dev host's paths -- install.sh resolves them for the machine it's actually installing on (PATH, then ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/local/bin, /usr/bin) and overwrites them in the freshly-generated config/sources.json, so these two values are placeholders, not a guarantee; run `make doctor` (or ./install.sh --doctor) any time to check every path this file has against what's actually on disk -- see INSTALL.md's "Tool & data path detection".
